root_cause.text: ocfs2 introduced an ABBA lock ordering bug by taking `ip_alloc_sem` before `ocfs2_del_inode_from_orphan()` in `ocfs2_dio_end_io_write()`, while `ocfs2_unlink()` already acquires the orphan-directory `inode_lock` and then `ip_alloc_sem`, creating a deadlock on `ocfs2_sysfile_lock_key[ORPHAN_DIR_SYSTEM_INODE]` vs. `ocfs2_file_ip_alloc_sem_key`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and patch show `ocfs2_unlink` locks `orphan_dir_inode` then `down_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem)`, whereas `ocfs2_dio_end_io_write` previously did `down_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem)` before calling `ocfs2_del_inode_from_orphan()` which takes `inode_lock(orphan_dir_inode)`; the fix moves `ocfs2_del_inode_from_orphan` out of the `ip_alloc_sem` critical section and deletes the earlier `down_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem)` placement.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unnecessary `ip_alloc_sem` write lock acquisition from the OCFS2 direct-IO write completion path to correct locking behavior.
intent_record.what: The call to `down_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem);` was removed from `ocfs2_dio_end_io_write()` just before the comment "Delete orphan before acquire i_rwsem." No other code in the hunk was changed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer takes the `ip_alloc_sem` write semaphore at this point in the direct-IO write completion path. This changes the locking order/locking coverage for the subsequent orphan-deletion and `i_rwsem`-related operations, likely avoiding unnecessary serialization or a lock ordering issue.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add allocation semaphore locking in direct I/O write completion to prevent races during inode extent handling.
intent_record.what: A write lock acquisition, `down_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem);`, was inserted immediately before reading `di_bh->b_data` and initializing the dinode extent tree in `ocfs2_dio_end_io_write()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this serializes the direct-I/O write completion path against concurrent allocation-related operations on the inode, preventing races while the on-disk dinode and extent tree are being accessed and updated.

The change adds ip_alloc_sem locking in direct I/O write completion, which matches the lock-order area involved in the ABBA deadlock root cause around ocfs2_dio_end_io_write() and ocfs2_unlink().

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix lock acquisition occurs before deleting the inode from the orphan list, creating the ABBA ordering with ocfs2_unlink() which takes the orphan-directory inode lock first and then ip_alloc_sem.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement acquires ip_alloc_sem before ocfs2_del_inode_from_orphan() in ocfs2_dio_end_io_write(), creating the ABBA lock order inversion with ocfs2_unlink(), which already takes the orphan directory inode lock and then ip_alloc_sem.

Take ip_alloc_sem to prevent concurrent access
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit a86a72a4a4e0ec109a98e2737948864ed6794bf7
Author: Ryan Ding <ryan.ding@oracle.com>
Date:   Fri Mar 25 14:21:18 2016 -0700

    ocfs2: take ip_alloc_sem in ocfs2_dio_get_block & ocfs2_dio_end_io_write
    
    Take ip_alloc_sem to prevent concurrent access to extent tree, which may
    cause the extent tree in an unstable state.
    
    Signed-off-by: Ryan Ding <ryan.ding@oracle.com>
    Reviewed-by: Junxiao Bi <junxiao.bi@oracle.com>
    Cc: Joseph Qi <joseph.qi@huawei.com>
    Cc: Mark F
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the problematic ordering in `ocfs2_dio_end_io_write()`: it now does `ret = ocfs2_inode_lock(inode, &di_bh, 1);` and then `down_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem);` before the comment `/* Delete orphan before acquire i_mutex. */` and the orphan handling path. This means `ip_alloc_sem` is taken inside the end-I/O write path before `ocfs2_del_inode_from_orphan()` is reached, matching the described ABBA ordering issue. The fix is not present here because there is no reordering to avoid the deadlock with `ocfs2_unlink()`'s `inode_lock`/`ip_alloc_sem` path; instead, this commit explicitly introduces `ip_alloc_sem` acquisition in this function. The added `up_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem);` only releases the lock later and does not address the lock-order inversion.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable ABBA pattern is not present in this commit version. In the new end-io path, `ocfs2_dio_end_io_write()` explicitly says `/* Delete orphan before acquire i_mutex. */` and calls `ocfs2_del_inode_from_orphan(osb, inode, di_bh, !!end, end);` before any `mutex_lock(&inode->i_mutex)`, which is the fix direction for the orphan-directory vs. inode lock ordering issue. Also, the direct I/O write path no longer performs orphan deletion inline in `ocfs2_direct_IO_write()`; instead `ocfs2_direct_IO()` passes `ocfs2_dio_end_io` and `ocfs2_dio_get_block`, and the old `ocfs2_direct_IO_write()` function body that contained the risky orphan cleanup path is removed from the diff. Therefore the buggy construct is absent here, and the fix is already present.
